brow: Aggregated snapshot · open-source compilation · not official reporting
editionNote: Morning edition. It covers the 24 hours to 05:10 CET on 25 October (clocks went back one hour overnight); new research covers 16:10 CET on 24 October to 05:10 CET on 25 October, items from the previous edition still inside the 24 hours were carried, and stories with new developments are marked as follow-ups.

theaters.heading: Battlefield, long-range strikes, and peace diplomacy in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: Mass Drone Swarm Strikes Central Belgorod in Russia Overnight
items.lede: Regional officials confirmed a large attack and told residents to shelter, while a monitoring channel said drones converged on MegaGRINN, the city's largest shopping complex.

sections.text: A large swarm of Ukrainian drones attacked the Russian city of Belgorod, near Ukraine's border, overnight into 25 October, and the regional operational headquarters confirmed a 'massive UAV attack' without naming targets, the Kyiv Independent reported [1]. The monitoring channel Exilenova Plus said the target was the MegaGRINN shopping complex, the city's largest, which was closed and empty at the time [1]. Residents reported a fire in a residential courtyard nearby [1]. The Kyiv Independent's updated report cited authorities saying one civilian was killed and 10 injured, while also noting Russian officials had not detailed damage or casualties [1]. The headquarters told residents to stay indoors as attacks continued [1]. No Ukrainian military claim was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is moderate that a large attack hit Belgorod, because regional officials confirmed it, but only one outlet was read. Confidence on the target and casualties is low, because the report is internally inconsistent and unverified.

items.title: Russian Drone Kills Three in an Apartment Block in Ukraine's Synelnykove
items.lede: The toll of injured rose to at least 12, an 11-year-old girl among them, as further drones killed one person in Kharkiv and showered debris on central Kyiv.

sections.text: A Russian drone struck a high-rise in Synelnykove, in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region, on the evening of 24 October, setting the fourth floor on fire and destroying a store and several cars, Governor Oleksandr Hanzha said [2][3]. Three people were killed [2][3]. Hanzha first reported at least eight injured, including an 11-year-old girl, and later at least 12, with two in serious condition undergoing surgery [2][3]. Later that night a jet-powered drone hit Kharkiv's Novobavarskyi district, killing one person and injuring four, Mayor Ihor Terekhov said [4]. Drone debris fell on a car park in central Kyiv, damaging cars and injuring one person, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said [5]. A strike on an energy facility cut power to one district of Vinnytsia region, with no injuries, its governor said [6]. The Air Force tally for the night was not published by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the Synelnykove deaths, because the governor is on record in two outlets; the injury count rose between reports. Confidence on the Kharkiv, Kyiv, and Vinnytsia details is moderate, because only Ukrinform was read.

items.title: Drones Reach Siberia's Omsk, 2,500 Kilometres From Ukraine, and Hit a Logistics Hub
items.lede: Omsk's governor confirmed a logistics hub was struck and staff evacuated, while a Ukrainian monitoring channel also reported a fire at a petrochemical plant tied to missile fuel.

sections.text: Drones attacked the Russian city of Omsk in Siberia, about 2,500 kilometres from Ukraine, on 24 October, Governor Vitaly Khotsenko said, adding that a logistics hub was hit, staff were evacuated, and emergency services were at the scene [7][8]. The Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova Plus said a fire broke out at the Omsky Kauchuk petrochemical plant, a maker of synthetic rubber that it tied to Iskander rocket fuel supply, and that a warehouse of online retailer Ozon was also hit [7]. The Kyiv Independent said it could not verify the reports [7]. No Ukrainian General Staff claim or Russian Defence Ministry tally for Omsk was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that drones struck Omsk, because the Russian governor confirmed it and two outlets report it. Confidence on the plant and Ozon hits is low, because they rest on a monitoring channel.

items.title: Blackout Hits Occupied Crimea After a Strike on Russia's Taman Substation
items.lede: The Russian-installed Sevastopol governor confirmed the outage, and power briefly returned before residents reported new cuts in several cities and internet monitors logged wide disruption.

sections.text: A blackout hit Russian-occupied Crimea in Ukraine overnight into 24 October after an attack on energy infrastructure, with outages reported in Sevastopol, Simferopol, Yalta, Feodosia, and other towns, monitoring channels said [9][10]. NASA FIRMS satellite data showed damage at the Taman substation in Russia's Krasnodar region, which links the peninsula to the Russian grid, the Kyiv Independent reported [10]. Sevastopol's Russian-installed governor Mikhail Razvozhayev confirmed the outage and said social facilities switched to backup power [9][10]. Local authorities later said power returned in several cities, but residents reported new outages in Simferopol, Yalta, and Alushta [10]. Crimea's Russian-installed head Sergei Aksyonov restricted electricity and water supplies, blaming a Ukrainian attack on main grids [11], and Russia's Energy Ministry said parts of occupied Kherson, Zaporizhzhia, Donetsk, and Luhansk regions were also without power [12]. Late on 24 October Razvozhayev said power had not been fully restored in Sevastopol, with about 40 percent of apartment buildings supplied and repairs outside the region continuing overnight [13]. NetBlocks reported wide internet outages [10]. No Ukrainian military claim for the Taman strike was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that a wide outage occurred, because the Russian-installed governor confirmed it. Confidence on the cause is moderate, because it rests on monitoring channels and satellite fire data.

items.title: Ukraine Says Starlink and Starshield Speeds Are Restored After Weeks of Caps
items.lede: President Zelensky thanked Congress, the State Department, and President Trump, while Elon Musk said the caps closed a 'loophole' he blamed on Ukraine's military.

sections.text: Ukraine's Defence Ministry said on 24 October that its monitoring recorded Starlink and Starshield working again at speeds above 400 kilometres per hour with a stable connection, after a cap of about 161 kilometres per hour in place since mid-October [14][15]. President Volodymyr Zelensky said in a video address that restoration began overnight and that checks after his morning briefing confirmed the systems worked [16]. A day earlier he had said the caps were still in place [15]. The Wall Street Journal reported that President Donald Trump ordered SpaceX chief Elon Musk on 21 October to lift the limits, while Trump said he had not spoken to Musk, the Kyiv Independent reported [15]. US Senator Richard Blumenthal opened a probe asking the Pentagon who ordered the restrictions [15]. Musk later wrote on X that Ukraine's military had 'violated Starlink terms of service and used it for offensive drone strikes to kill people,' adding: 'That loophole was closed last week'; presidential adviser Serhii Beskrestnov disputed this, the Kyiv Independent reported [15].

Confidence is high that Ukraine reports restored speeds, because the Defence Ministry and the president are on record in two outlets. Confidence on who ordered the caps is low, because Musk defended the caps but no party has said who ordered them lifted.

items.title: Ukraine's General Staff Claims Hits on Plants in Oryol and Tolyatti and a Yeysk Aircraft
items.lede: Kyiv's military says the Oryol plant builds parts for Iskander missiles and the Tolyatti site makes rubber for solid rocket fuel, while damage to the aircraft is still being assessed.

sections.text: Ukraine's General Staff said on 24 October that its forces hit the main production building of Proton-Elektrotex in Oryol, Russia, which it said makes modules for S-71 Kover air-launched cruise missiles, parts for Iskander-M missiles, and Pantsir-S1 components [17]. It said the Tolyattikauchuk synthetic rubber plant in Tolyatti, Samara region, was also struck, with an explosion and fire nearby, and that the rubber is used in solid rocket fuel [17][18]. An aircraft at Yeysk airfield in Krasnodar region was hit, with damage still being assessed [17][18]. The Oryol plant was first struck during the 23 October drone raid that closed Moscow's airports, the Kyiv Independent reported [19]. Tolyatti Mayor Ilya Sukhikh said industrial facilities were damaged, with no deaths or injuries according to preliminary reports, but did not say which; local authorities near Yeysk confirmed an attack but reported only minor damage to two apartment buildings, without mentioning the airfield, Reuters reported [20].

Confidence is moderate, because the claims come from Ukraine's military, a party to the war; two outlets carry the General Staff claims; Russian officials confirmed damage in Tolyatti but not to the plant, and denied nothing at Yeysk beyond residential damage.

items.title: Russian Missile Kills a Man at a Warehouse in Ukraine's Kharkiv Region
items.lede: Doctors could not save a 45-year-old man, two other men were hospitalised, and emergency crews fought the fire that followed.

sections.text: A Russian missile struck a warehouse in Lozova, in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, on 24 October, starting a fire, Governor Oleh Syniehubov said [21]. A 45-year-old man died of his injuries, and two men aged 26 and 43 were hospitalised [21]. Russian forces attacked Kharkiv city and 15 other settlements in the region over the past day, injuring seven people including two children [21]. No Russian statement on the target was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the casualties, because the governor is on record. Confidence is moderate overall, because no second outlet was found.

items.title: Zelensky Blacklists 51 People and 44 Firms Behind Russia's Ballistic Missiles
items.lede: The first list targets suppliers of Iskander, Kalibr, Kh-101, and Kinzhal weapons, including Russia's sole maker of some composite parts for defence plants.

sections.text: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky signed decrees on 24 October enacting National Security and Defence Council sanctions on Russian entities and people who help make ballistic missiles or supply Russia's arms industry with parts for aircraft, armoured vehicles, missile systems, and drones, his office said [22]. The first list names 51 individuals and 44 entities tied to weapons such as the Iskander, Kalibr, Kh-101, and Kinzhal [22][23]. Targets include the G. S. Petrov Institute of Plastics and the Kometa space systems corporation [22]. No Russian response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that the decrees were signed and on the list's size, because the presidential office is on record and two outlets agree.

items.title: Russia Sends 126 Drones at Ukraine Overnight, Nearly Half of Them Jet-Powered
items.lede: Air defences stopped 101 of them, but one hit a Kyiv apartment block, and regional officials counted four dead and 78 hurt over the past day.

sections.text: Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched 126 attack and decoy drones, 61 of them jet-powered, from 18:00 Kyiv time on 23 October, and that 101 were shot down or suppressed by 08:00 on 24 October [24][25]. It recorded hits at 14 locations and falling debris at five [24]. Early on 24 October a drone struck a residential building in Kyiv's Obolon district, injuring two and starting a fire, the city administration said [25]. Regional officials reported four killed and 78 injured across Ukraine over the past day, including deaths in Kramatorsk, Sloviansk, and Dnipro, and nine injured in Zhytomyr [25]. No Russian Defence Ministry statement on the overnight targets was read by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the drone tally and casualties, because the Air Force and regional officials are on record and two outlets agree. Confidence on the Air Force interception figures is moderate, because they are a party's own count.

items.title: Trump Floats 200% Tariffs on Ukraine and Russia, Then Doubts They Would Work
items.lede: At a Florida rally he said it had not occurred to him before, then conceded the US buys too little from either country for the threat to bite.

sections.text: US President Donald Trump told a campaign rally in Florida that 'probably we should do that immediately with Ukraine and Russia', referring to 200% tariffs he said had ended other wars, a Ukrinform correspondent reported [26]. He then said 'we don't buy enough to do it for them' [26]. Trump has said before that the threat of such tariffs ended fighting between India and Pakistan, which India denies [26]. No White House follow-up or Ukrainian or Russian reply was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that Trump said this, because a correspondent attended. Confidence on any policy step is low, because he gave no plan and doubted the idea himself.

items.title: Romania Halts the Search for Three Sailors From the Sunken Khoryv at Dusk
items.lede: Poor visibility ended nearly four hours of renewed searching on Saturday evening, and maritime coordinators announced no date to resume.

sections.text: A drone strike sank the Comoros-flagged cargo ship Khoryv about 13 nautical miles off Romania's port of Constanta, just outside Romanian territorial waters, on 23 October, Reuters reported [1]. Romania's naval authority said nine of the 13 Ukrainian and Azeri crew were rescued, one body was recovered, and three were missing [1][2]. President Nicusor Dan called it part of Russia's escalation in its war in Ukraine [1]. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned another Russian escalation in the Black Sea [3]. Reuters counts at least seven cargo ships hit off Romania and Bulgaria in two weeks, with some 30 sailors dead or missing, mostly near the Sulina Canal, Ukraine's main Danube export route [1]. Dan said Romania will receive additional military equipment after a Supreme Defence Council meeting and a NATO committee session requested by Romania and Bulgaria [4]. A Romanian Interior Ministry Black Hawk joined the renewed search on 24 October [5][6]. The Maritime Coordination Centre suspended it at 18:04 local time (16:04 CET) for poor visibility and set no restart date [6]. No Russian response was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the sinking, toll, and suspended search, because Romanian authorities and several outlets agree. Confidence on Russian responsibility is moderate, because no forensic findings were published.

items.title: Moldova Identifies the Downed Drone as a Russian Geran-4 and Destroys Its Warhead
items.lede: Army and police experts secured the crash site overnight before defusing the explosive charge, and the ministry urged residents not to touch any debris.

sections.text: Moldova expelled a Russian diplomat on 23 October after a Russian Geran drone came down near family homes and an energy facility, President Maia Sandu said, calling it Russia's latest dangerous act [7]. Police said a resident found the drone in Kistelnita village, Telenesti district, about 100 metres from a house [7]. Moldova's Defence Ministry said a drone entered its airspace at 13:59 local time (11:59 CET) during a large Russian attack on Ukraine, crossing from Ukraine's Vinnytsia region toward Moldova's Russian-controlled Transnistria region before vanishing from radar [7]. Moldova also logged several Russian drone incursions on 16 October [7]. On 24 October Moldova's Defence Ministry said a joint army and Interior Ministry team identified the drone as a Geran-4, secured the site overnight, and defused and destroyed its warhead [8]. No Russian response was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high that the drone fell, was identified, and was made safe, because police and the Defence Ministry are on record. Confidence is moderate on the expulsion details, because only one outlet was read.

items.title: Bulgaria Plans a Black Sea Security Hub in Varna and Constanta With French Backing
items.lede: Foreign Minister Velislava Petrova tied the plan to recent drone strikes on merchant ships, and France's Jean-Noel Barrot called it an EU project against hybrid attacks.

sections.text: Bulgaria's Foreign Minister Velislava Petrova said on 24 October that a Black Sea security hub will be set up in Varna and in Romania's port of Constanta, based at Bulgaria's Naval Academy in Varna, after visiting it with French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot [9][10]. She said the partnership with Romania focuses on hybrid and cyber threats, that the base needs more infrastructure, and that French and EU funding matter [9]. Petrova said a run of attacks on merchant ships in recent weeks showed the sea becoming part of the war, and she called for a moratorium on such attacks [9]. Barrot said the maritime security platform is an EU project to defend the eastern flank against hybrid attacks, that a 22nd sanctions package is being prepared, and that Russia is blocking a moratorium that President Zelensky is open to [9]. Bulgaria and France also signed a road map for their strategic partnership [9]. No timeline or budget for the hub was given, and no Russian response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that the ministers announced the hub, because the state news agency BTA quoted both on the record, though bTV only relays BTA. Details on funding and start date are not yet public.

items.title: Storm Boelo Brings 75mph Gusts and Flooded Roads to Scotland
items.lede: Amber wind warnings for northern England and Scotland run until 21:00 UK time (22:00 CET) on Sunday, while more than 2,000 homes in north-west England lost power overnight.
items.flag: FOLLOW UP TO PREVIOUS REPORT · single-source, unconfirmed

sections.text: Storm Boelo, the UK's second named storm in two days after Storm Austen, brought gusts of 75mph to the Western Isles by Saturday evening as amber wind warnings came into force for Scotland, northern England, and parts of Northern Ireland, the BBC reported [1]. The Met Office warned of danger to life from flying debris and large waves [1]. Network Rail closed several Scottish routes, LNER advised against travel between Edinburgh and Aberdeen on Sunday, and Stena Line, Irish Ferries, and P&O Ferries cancelled Irish Sea crossings [2]. Train and ferry services were cancelled in Scotland, police warned against unnecessary journeys, and flooding closed roads including the A78 in Greenock and the A77 at Lendalfoot [1]. The Northern Ireland amber warning runs until 10:00 UK time (11:00 CET) on Sunday [1]. National Grid said more than 124,000 properties had been reconnected since Storm Austen, though hundreds in south-west England were still without power on Saturday evening [1]. Events in England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland were cancelled [2].
Confidence is high on the warnings, closures, and power figures, because the BBC attributes them to the Met Office, Network Rail, and National Grid; only BBC pages were read.

items.title: Milan Prosecutors Detain Alleged Mastermind of Italy's Movimento 17 Ottobre
items.lede: Youssef Siher, a 30-year-old researcher, faces suspected incitement with terrorist aims and organised protest violence under the new decree, and his wife is also under investigation.

sections.text: Italian police on Saturday night detained Youssef Siher, a 30-year-old Italian researcher considered the mastermind of the Movimento 17 ottobre linked to last weekend's clashes in central Milan, on the order of Milan prosecutors, ANSA reported [3]. He is suspected of incitement to commit crimes aggravated by terrorist aims and of organised violence at public demonstrations under Article 420 bis of the new decree [3]. His wife is under investigation without arrest for the same offences [3]. Earlier he had been questioned at Milan police headquarters while a home was searched, Corriere della Sera reported, citing Tg1 [4]. The 500 Folgore paratroopers sent under the decree patrolled central Milan alongside police, and police took a group of youths from Piazza Duomo for checks [4][5]. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said the decree's measures aim to stop violent people setting cities ablaze while guaranteeing the right to protest, and thanked police and Interior Minister Matteo Piantedosi [6]. No national arrest figure was confirmed by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the detention and the charges, because ANSA reports the prosecutors' order; the earlier questioning rests on Corriere citing Tg1.

items.title: France Arrests Nearly 1,000 as Night Clashes Follow Calmer Nationwide Marches
items.lede: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez counted 410,000 marchers against 550,000 a week earlier and said two people were seriously hurt, in Toulouse and Clermont-Ferrand.

sections.text: French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said on Saturday evening that police had made nearly 1,000 arrests, against 385 at the same time on 17 Oct, and that the figure would rise [7][8][9]. He counted 410,000 people at 289 events, against 550,000 at 430 a week earlier; the CGT said 800,000 [9][10]. He said marches passed off well but black-clad ultra-left groups attacked police with an extremely elevated level of violence, while no public buildings were attacked and looting was very limited [8][9]. In Toulouse, a 20-year-old man suffered a serious hand injury during a dispersal, the prefecture said, and it reported 30 arrests and 27 people in custody [10][9]. Marseille's prefecture reported 51 arrests, 20 in custody, and three shops looted as barricades burned [9][11]. In Tours, a bank branch was set on fire and eight police officers were injured, the prefecture said [12]. Nuñez said far-right activists sought clashes in Cannes and Montpellier for the first time and that police would stay on high alert overnight [8]. No final overnight national arrest or custody count was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the national and local figures, because Nuñez and the prefectures spoke on record and AFP, the BBC, and TF1 report them; the overnight total is not yet published.

items.title: Belgian Interior Minister Thanks Police After Brussels and Liège Protests End
items.lede: Police detained nine of about 400 Brussels protesters and five in Liège, far fewer than the 150 arrests of the previous weekend.

sections.text: A few hundred people gathered on Saturday at the Mont des Arts in Brussels, Belgium, and youths heading for the liberal MR party's headquarters broke a police cordon in Saint-Gilles, where riot police fired tear gas on Chaussée de Forest [13][14][15]. Police pushed them back towards Brussels-South station, and protesters tried to set a pile of shared scooters alight before the last of them were kettled at Square de l'Aviation [15][16]. Reuters witnesses saw officers hit and kick one demonstrator during a chase [17]. Brussels police said about 400 people took part; five were detained for disturbing public order and four arrested over prohibited weapons and incitement to violence [18][16]. In Liège, about 200 marchers briefly blocked access to the A602 motorway, and police made five arrests [16][18]. Belgian Interior Minister Bernard Quintin said on X that the protests ended without major incident, thanked police for their firmness, and said those behind damage and fires must be identified and punished [18]. No injury figures were found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the clashes and the arrest figures, because Belga, RTBF, La Libre, and Reuters report them and the police and Quintin spoke on record.

items.title: Trappes Gunman Had Booby-Trapped His Flat, French Anti-Terror Prosecutors Say
items.lede: His custody was extended on Saturday and four relatives and friends, including his mother, were being questioned, while the wounded 12-year-old girl remains in critical condition.

sections.text: France's National Anti-Terrorism Prosecutor's Office (Pnat) said on Saturday that the custody of Kévin T., 39, was extended after Friday's drive-by shooting in Trappes and La Verrière, west of Paris, which killed one man and wounded five, an attack President Macron called "a racist terrorist attack" [19][20]. Three people from his family and friends were taken into custody on Friday night and overnight, bringing to four the relatives questioned, among them his mother, AFP reported [20][19]. A search found his flat in Plaisir rigged with gas bottles and electrical wires connected to a timer, a police source told AFP; a Sten submachine gun and a tear-gas canister were found in his Renault Clio [20]. A copy of Mein Kampf was found at his home, and he reportedly tested positive for cocaine, RTL reported, citing sources [19]. The Pnat said the girl, hit by eight bullets, is still in critical condition [20]. The Pnat is investigating murder and attempted murder linked to a terrorist enterprise, aggravated by racial or religious motive [20][19]. No charge was announced by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the custody, the investigation, and the girl's condition, because the Pnat spoke on record to AFP; the booby-trap, Mein Kampf, and cocaine details rest on unnamed sources.

items.title: Spanish Minister Condemns People's Party Deepfake Ad Targeting Sánchez's Wife
items.lede: Leire Díez, a former Socialist member, has gone to court over the clip, which drew nearly 2 million views, while the PP calls it satire.

sections.text: Spain's conservative People's Party (PP) posted a campaign video this week using artificial intelligence to show people linked to Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's Socialists appearing to admit wrongdoing, The Guardian reported [21]. A deepfake of Sánchez's wife, Begoña Gómez, speaks about getting a university post through her husband, and one of former Prime Minister José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero speaks about hiding jewellery, nods to investigations in which both deny wrongdoing [21]. The video had nearly 2 million views by Friday and carried a tiny, near-transparent AI label [21]. Digital Transformation Minister Óscar López told TVE on Friday it was "a colossal lie" and "intolerable" on a party's official accounts [21]. Former Socialist member Leire Díez filed a court complaint on Friday alleging defamation and digital identity theft, the paper reported [21]. PP official Borja Sémper said the video highlighted Socialist hypocrisy and was not meant to deceive [21]. Most legal experts consulted by El País said it was not illegal [21]. Spain votes on 29 November [21].
Confidence is high on the video and the quoted reactions, because The Guardian cites named officials on record; the Díez complaint rests on reported accounts, and no court record was read.

items.title: Foreign Drone Wreckage Found in Latvian Forest Near the Russian Border
items.lede: The aircraft apparently came down on 18 October unnoticed, and Latvia's armed forces have opened an internal review of why no public alert was sent.

sections.text: Police found the wreckage of a foreign unmanned aircraft in a forest in Liepna parish, Alūksne municipality, in eastern Latvia, on the morning of 24 October after a tip from residents, LSM and Delfi reported [1] [2]. The National Armed Forces (NBS) said residents had reported an explosion-like noise there on 18 October, and radar data later showed a possible unidentified object in Latvian airspace, but a two-day search was called off [1] [3]. The NBS said the data then did not meet the criteria for a mobile-phone alert and has opened an internal review of the decisions taken [2] [3]. No one was hurt and no civilian infrastructure was damaged [1]. Defence Minister Raivis Melnis told Latvian Radio that Ukraine struck Russian targets on 18 October and that, if the drone is Ukrainian, it may have been hit over Russia and glided in, adding that gaps in eastern air defence must be closed [1]. The drone's origin has not been officially confirmed.
Confidence is high on the find, the 18 October timeline, and the review, which LSM, Delfi, and BB.LV attribute to the NBS and police; the Ukrainian origin is the minister's hypothesis.

items.title: Lithuania Hosts NATO Reserves Committee for the First Time
items.lede: Vice-minister Karolis Aleksa told about 50 allied and partner delegates, including Ukraine, that reservists must be ready to reinforce regular forces from a war's first days.

sections.text: Lithuania's Ministry of National Defence said on 24 October that the NATO Committee on Reserves, an advisory body to the NATO Military Committee, met in Lithuania for the first time this week in Vilnius [4]. About 50 representatives of NATO commands, member states, and partners, including Ukraine, Australia, and Switzerland, discussed reserve readiness and integration into collective-defence plans [4]. Vice-minister Karolis Aleksa presented Lithuania's reserve reform, citing Russia's war on Ukraine, the national division under development, and the German brigade Lithuania is receiving, and said the country is steadily increasing reservist numbers and training [4]. The ministry gave no reservist figures.
Confidence is moderate, because the account comes only from the ministry's own release, which LRT relays; the meeting dates within the week were not stated.

items.title: Estonia Budgets €13.5 Million to Host the Ukraine Recovery Conference
items.lede: The Tallinn gathering on 28–29 January will draw thousands of delegates, and a 16-member project team under Tiit Riisalo is organising it.

sections.text: Estonia's government set the budget for the 2027 Ukraine Recovery Conference (URC27) in Tallinn at €13.5 million, conference media manager Reimo Raja confirmed to ERR on 24 October [5]. Nearly all ministries and several agencies are involved, and the Foreign Ministry's deputy secretary general Mariin Ratnik oversees the work [5]. Raja said a preliminary Rebuild Ukraine conference will be held in Warsaw on 12–13 November with an EU-Ukraine Investment Forum, which Economy Minister Liina Vahtras will attend, and that several key participants have confirmed for Tallinn [5].
Confidence is moderate, because only ERR reports the figure, though it quotes the conference's own spokesman.

items.title: Bulgaria Elects a President Sunday as Diaspora Voting Opens Overnight
items.lede: Police logged 168 election-law complaints by Saturday afternoon, 143 of them about vote-buying, as about 6.5 million voters choose among 27 tickets.

sections.text: Bulgaria holds its presidential and vice-presidential election on 25 October, with 27 candidate pairs and about 6.5 million registered voters; polls open from 07:00 to 20:00 local time [1]. Voting abroad began at 21:00 Bulgarian time on 24 October in Auckland and ends at 05:00 on 26 October in California and Nevada, at 613 polling stations in 60 countries, including 82 in the UK and 70 in Germany, the Foreign Ministry said via BTA [2] [1]. The Interior Ministry said it had received 168 reports of election-law violations since the campaign began, 143 of them on vote-buying, opened six criminal proceedings, and issued 1,226 warning protocols as of 14:00 on 24 October [3]. The previous presidential election went to a run-off in November 2021 [1].
Confidence is high on the election arrangements, which BTA and N1 report consistently; the violation figures are the Interior Ministry's own and are reports, not findings.

items.title: Albanian Police Fire Tear Gas as Protesters Stone Tirana's Education Ministry
items.lede: Prime Minister Edi Rama promised a reflection on the protesters' message within hours or days, but warned the state's response to violence would be prolonged.

sections.text: On 24 October, the 12th day of protests in Tirana, Albania, opposition Democratic Party supporters led by Sali Berisha rallied outside the prime minister's office and burned the chairs and pillows Rama had left there as an invitation to dialogue, then marched to the Ministry of Education [4] [5]. A student protest began there at 14:00 local time (13:00 CET); groups threw stones at the building and at police, who answered with water cannon and tear gas, the state agency ATA reported [4]. Rama said his government would present its overall reflection within hours or days, while vowing a persistent state response to those who commit or glorify violence [5]. State Police reported 271 arrests over the first seven days [6][7]. The Health Ministry put injuries at 310, including 191 police officers, on 19 October [8], and official data showed 320 injured, including 192 police officers, by 21 October [7]. The Health Ministry said 13 people, including protesters, police officers, and two journalists, were treated for injuries by 19:45 local time (18:45 CET) on Saturday [9]; the protest ended about 21:15 local time (20:15 CET), with several people detained [10].
Confidence is high on Saturday's clashes, remarks, and injuries, which ATA, Euronews, and Albeu report consistently; official arrest totals run only to 21 October.

items.title: Serbia Votes Sunday After an Election Eve of Media and Fraud Complaints
items.lede: Independent members of the media regulator REM say a notice accusing N1 and Nova of breaking the campaign silence was issued without the council's approval.

sections.text: Serbia's election silence has been in force since midnight on 22–23 October and bans campaigning and result estimates until polls close at 20:00 on 25 October [11] [12]. Serbia's 6,450,523 voters choose among 18 lists for 250 seats [11] [13]. The BBC said analysts expect an extremely tight vote between Aleksandar Vučić's SNS and the Student List [14]. On 24 October the pro-government Informer reported N1 and Nova to the regulator REM for covering a story linking top officials to criminals during the silence; REM issued a notice of violation, but council member Rodoljub Šabić said none of the independent members had seen or approved it, N1 reported [15]. The Journalists' Association of Serbia (UNS) said foreign reporters had received no accreditation decisions and that the election commission and ministry did not answer its questions [16]. In Kladovo, requests to vote outside polling stations rose from 115 to 425 in a day, and an opposition commission member reported the case to police on suspicion that voters were registered without consent, N1 reported, citing the portal Mašina [17].

Confidence is high on the silence rules and voter figures; the REM, accreditation, and Kladovo complaints rest on N1, an outlet named in the REM notice, and were not answered by the authorities by the cutoff.

items.title: Bosnia's Presidency Chair Bećirović Hails a New Chapter With Hungary's Magyar Government
items.lede: Meeting Prime Minister Péter Magyar in Budapest, Denis Bećirović said the previous Hungarian government's policy had damaged trust between the two states.

sections.text: Denis Bećirović, chairman of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina, met Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar in Budapest on 24 October, Sarajevo Times reported, citing a statement from Bećirović's office [18]. They discussed bilateral relations, economic and security cooperation, and European and Euro-Atlantic integration [18]. Bećirović said the meeting marked the start of a new phase, that the previous Hungarian government's policy had damaged mutual trust, and that political change in Hungary offered a chance for cooperation based on European values [18]. He welcomed the new government's support for EU enlargement, said full EU and NATO membership remains Bosnia's strategic goal, and pointed to room for Hungarian investment in energy, industry, IT, food, and tourism [18]. No Hungarian readout was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because the account rests on the Bosnian presidency chair's own statement as relayed by one outlet; Hungary's view of the talks is not known.

items.title: Hundreds March in Georgia's Capital Against Ivanishvili's One-Party Rule
items.lede: The weekly march extends a protest movement now past 700 days, which demands new parliamentary elections and the release of about 150 prisoners of conscience.

sections.text: Hundreds of people marched through central Tbilisi, Georgia, on the evening of 24 October carrying Georgian, EU, and Ukrainian flags, in the traditional Saturday march against Georgian Dream founder Bidzina Ivanishvili, JAMnews reported [1]. The main slogan was “Georgia against Ivanishvili's one-party rule!” [1]. Protesters demand a return to European integration, the release of political prisoners, repeal of laws passed by Georgian Dream over the past two years, and early parliamentary elections [1]. JAMnews said dozens of protesters have been arrested over nearly two years and that Georgia holds around 150 prisoners of conscience, including journalist Mzia Amaglobeli [1]. No incidents or detentions were reported for Saturday's march.
Confidence is moderate, because the account rests on one JAMnews report; the crowd size is its own estimate and no police figure was found.

items.title: Armenia Reports Arrests in Vote-Buying Probes on the Eve of Local Elections
items.lede: The Anti-Corruption Committee confirmed detentions in several communities, with party candidates and a community head reported held, before Sunday's polls in 21 communities.

sections.text: Armenia's Anti-Corruption Committee confirmed on 24 October that criminal proceedings over election-related corruption offenses are under way in several communities and that some people have been arrested, Armenpress reported [2]. The committee said evidence-gathering and other procedural actions were being carried out but gave no further details, citing the preliminary investigation [2]. According to media reports cited by Armenpress, members and council candidates of the For the Republic and Homeland parties were detained in Artik, representatives of the Our Community alliance in Martuni, and the community head, his deputy, and council members in Yeghegnadzor [2]. Local self-government elections are held in 21 Armenian communities on 25 October [2]. No arrest total or charges had been published by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the committee's confirmation is official, but the names of those detained come from unnamed media reports relayed by Armenpress alone.

items.title: Georgia's Kobakhidze Visits Budapest as Guest of Orbán's Successor Magyar
items.lede: It was the Georgian Dream premier's first trip to Hungary since his close ally Viktor Orbán lost April's election to Péter Magyar's party.

sections.text: Georgian Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze attended events in Budapest, Hungary, on 23 October marking the 70th anniversary of the 1956 anti-Soviet uprising, including a gala concert and an official reception hosted by Prime Minister Péter Magyar, Civil Georgia reported on 24 October, citing Georgian government releases [3]. Other guests included European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, European Council President António Costa, Moldovan President Maia Sandu, and Ukraine's parliament speaker Ruslan Stefanchuk, while media reported many European leaders stayed away despite invitations [3]. Kobakhidze later told journalists he had held extensive discussions with Magyar on bilateral relations at an official dinner and hoped close cooperation would continue [4]. No Hungarian government statement on talks with Kobakhidze was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the attendance, which rests on the Georgian government's published photographs as reported by Civil Georgia; Kobakhidze says they discussed bilateral relations at dinner; Budapest has issued no readout.

items.title: Police Use Pepper Spray as Stuttgart Rally Backs Jailed Elbit Raid Suspects
items.lede: Three officers were hurt, one unable to keep working, as a largely peaceful march of 600 to 700 people turned tense at times.

sections.text: Several hundred people marched through central Stuttgart, Germany, on Saturday under the slogan 'Free the Ulm 5', in solidarity with pro-Palestinian activists jailed over an attack on the Ulm site of Israeli arms firm Elbit [1] [2]. Police counted 600 to 700 participants; organisers said about 1,000, and the Left party took part alongside pro-Palestinian and anti-war groups [1] [2]. Police wrote on X that several offences led to arrests, that officers were attacked, pyrotechnics were set off, and participants masked themselves, and that renewed attacks led them to use pepper spray [2]. Three officers were hurt, one unfit for duty, and paint bags were thrown at police [2]. The five defendants, three women and two men aged 25 to 40 with Irish, British, Spanish, and German nationality, are on trial at Stuttgart regional court for property damage, trespass, and alleged membership of a criminal organisation [1]. They are accused of breaking into the firm at night in September last year and causing damage in the millions [1]. No arrest count was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the march, the crowd estimates, and the charges, because dpa and SWR report them citing police and the court. Confidence is moderate on the clashes, which rest on police statements relayed by SWR.

items.title: Youth Wing Chief Urges Klingbeil to Give Up the SPD Leadership
items.lede: The Social Democrats elect a new executive in January, and the party's youth leader says he has seen no clear revival strategy from the finance minister.

sections.text: Philipp Türmer, who leads the Jusos, the youth wing of Germany's Social Democrats (SPD), said Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil should not run again for party chair if he wants to stay finance minister and vice-chancellor [3]. Türmer told the Neue Osnabrücker Zeitung he had seen 'no clear strategy' from Klingbeil for lifting the party, that the double role made that 'hardly possible', and that 'everything speaks for' a change [3] [4]. He named former labour minister Hubertus Heil and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania premier Manuela Schwesig as possible alternatives, while saying he would not commit to names yet [3] [4]. Bremen mayor Andreas Bovenschulte backed Klingbeil, telling the RedaktionsNetzwerk Deutschland he saw 'no need for change' [3]. Co-chair and labour minister Bärbel Bas announced her exit on 12 October, and Klingbeil said the whole leadership would stand for election [3] [4]. The vote is set for a party congress in Bremen on 16 and 17 January; Klingbeil has left a new candidacy open, and no official candidates have declared [3] [4].

Confidence is high on what Türmer and Bovenschulte said, because tagesschau and DER SPIEGEL quote them directly from named newspaper interviews. Confidence is low on whether Klingbeil will run again, which he has left open.

items.title: Merz Stays Silent on Aigner's Candidacy as CSU Delegates Cheer Her
items.lede: CSU leader Markus Söder wants the Union and the SPD to settle the presidential candidate in November, while CDU women push for one of their own.

sections.text: Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) closed the CSU party congress in Munich, Germany, on Saturday before some 700 delegates but said nothing about the CSU's push for Bavarian Landtag President Ilse Aigner as federal president [5] [6]. Merz mentioned Aigner right after Markus Söder at the start of his speech, setting off a storm of cheering as almost all delegates rose from their seats [5]. In a report from the congress, Söder said the CSU had 'never in 75 years' held neither the chancellery nor the presidency, and that a joint Union and SPD decision would best come 'now in November' [7]. CDU women are pressing for a woman from their own ranks, and the CDU says it holds the right to nominate [7] [8]; the federal assembly elects Frank-Walter Steinmeier's successor on 30 January 2027 [5]. Merz said anyone who thinks of giving the AfD their vote 'has no place in our Union', urged the SPD to implement agreed reforms 'now', and repeated that the electricity tax must fall for all consumers [5] [6] [9].

Confidence is high on what Merz and Söder said, because tagesschau, dpa, and Stuttgarter Zeitung quote them directly. Confidence is moderate on the CDU position and CSU frustration, which rest on unnamed party circles reported by tagesschau.

items.title: Storm Luise Injures Several in Western Germany as Manja Approaches
items.lede: Forecasters now expect hurricane gusts up to 130 km/h on the North Sea by Sunday afternoon, with Föhr and Erfurt taking precautions.

sections.text: Storm Luise left damage mainly in western and southwestern Germany on Friday and overnight, with police and fire crews called out in several states, mostly for fallen trees [10]. In Nastätten, Rhineland-Palatinate, a gust toppled a frame near an October market, seriously injuring two people; one is in critical condition and was flown to hospital [10] [11]. Near Aachen an ICE with 280 passengers stalled after overhead-line damage and was towed to Stolberg station [10]. Trains also halted at Karlsruhe main station and near Pforzheim [12] [13]. Baden-Württemberg police and fire crews handled more than 130 call-outs around Karlsruhe and Mannheim; a branch struck a cyclist in Kronau, causing minor injuries [14]. For Manja, the weather service now warns of hurricane gusts up to 130 km/h on some peaks and the North Sea, above all in Schleswig-Holstein, peaking on Sunday afternoon [15]. Hamburg's lower Fischmarkt could flood in a storm surge, Heligoland fast ferries are suspended, Wyk on Föhr has closed its harbour dyke gate, and Erfurt has shut its cemeteries for the weekend [10] [15]. No overnight damage reports for Manja were found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on the incidents, because tagesschau, dpa, and SWR cite police and fire services. Confidence is moderate on the Manja forecast, which rests on weather service projections.

items.title: Fire Largely Destroys Hitler's Former Eagle's Nest Tea House in Bavaria
items.lede: Prosecutors say the arrested suspect shows signs of mental illness and want him held in a psychiatric unit, while a political motive is still being examined.

sections.text: A fire late on Friday almost completely destroyed the Kehlsteinhaus, the Nazi-era tea house known as the Eagle's Nest above Berchtesgaden in Bavaria, Germany [16] [17]. First crews reached the mountain restaurant, at over 1,800 metres, at 21:52 local time (20:52 CET) on Friday; about 200 responders fought the blaze in rain and snow, and nobody was inside [16] [18]. Police arrested a 33-year-old German who met the fire crews on a motorcycle on the steep access road and, according to dpa, tried to flee [16] [17]. Traunstein prosecutor Rainer Vietze said a short psychiatric assessment found concrete signs of mental illness; the man was brought before a Rosenheim judge on Saturday, with prosecutors seeking his placement in a forensic psychiatric unit [16]. A possible political motive is being examined, but investigators are at the very beginning, Vietze said [16]. The head of the local operating association put the damage 'in the millions', and it is unclear whether the building can be restored [17]. Finished in 1938 inside the sealed-off Nazi leadership area, the building has been a restaurant since 1952 [18].

Confidence is high on the destruction, the arrest, and the prosecutor's statements, because tagesschau and ORF report the Berchtesgaden press conference. Confidence is moderate on the escape attempt, which rests on dpa information.

items.title: Wadephul Says Istanbul Group Will Meet Regularly, Next Time in Germany
items.lede: The eight countries took no concrete decisions but agreed to work together to get Russian and Ukrainian grain out by new Black Sea routes, the minister said.

sections.text: Germany's Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul (CDU) met his counterparts from France, Britain, Italy, Turkey, Egypt, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia in Istanbul on Friday, the first meeting in this format, held at German and Turkish initiative [19] [20]. Afterwards he said it went 'better than we had dared to hope', that the eight agreed to meet regularly, and that the next meeting will be in Germany, though no concrete decisions were taken [21] [22]. He said the group agreed to work together so that both Russian and Ukrainian grain can be exported and new Black Sea routes found [22]. Wadephul said the eight were jointly sending a signal that they would not accept Iran and the Houthis 'blackmailing world trade', and urged Putin to end attacks on Black Sea grain shipments [20] [21]. A joint press release from the eight on 24 October said they discussed freedom of navigation and tensions in the Straits of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb and the Black Sea, backed dialogue and de-escalation, and would continue the format; it did not mention grain routes or a German venue [23].

Confidence is high on the meeting, because ARD, Anadolu, Reuters, the German Foreign Office, and the joint press release report it. The grain routes and the German venue rest on Wadephul's own statements.
